claims.claim: Nutrien sits in the food-system chain potash/nitrogen/phosphate -> crop nutrient availability -> farm yields -> food supply, with large-scale potash production and distribution providing structural exposure to a resource bottleneck that cannot be eliminated by software or automation alone.

Mine automation and sub-$60/t controllable potash cash cost can improve resilience and throughput, but the successor bottlenecks remain commodity pricing, geology/capacity utilization, energy/input costs, logistics and farmer affordability.

risks.risk: Structural necessity of fertilizer does not guarantee stable company economics because benchmark prices and farmer affordability mediate value capture.

unknowns.unknown: Normalized long-run potash price and automation productivity are not established by the current evidence window.

claims.claim: Record first-half potash volumes and stronger earnings are compatible with genuine execution, but higher global fertilizer benchmarks are a material external tailwind and prevent attributing the full earnings improvement to operating skill.
The structural food-security thesis survives a commodity down-cycle counterfactual, while Nutrien's earnings power may not; this separates durable human need from cyclical value capture.

risks.risk: Commodity-price normalization can compress margins even if physical demand and volumes remain healthy.
Natural-gas/input costs, weather, geopolitics and farmer economics can create correlated volatility across fertilizer segments.

unknowns.unknown: Through-cycle earnings sensitivity by fertilizer benchmark remains an Alpha-owned underwriting gap.
